lines: `compute_reference` tests PROPORTIONALITY and never LEVEL; a line 43.6x too steep is perfectly proportional and qualified at 0.2% mean error.
An arm on an IMPORTED branch is not a failure of this gate -- it passed the same level bar, on another arm's ladder -- but it is an ASSUMPTION, and V3's cross-BN spread is what stands behind it.

gates.name: V3 references agree across BN
gates.prediction: the arms' compute references describe one machine
gates.rule: max/min implied TFLOP/s across BN <= 2.0x, on the RAW rates against the fixed roof
gates.observed: 1.94x raw (fixed roof, the gate input); 2.14x normalised to each arm's own clock (record, not the gate input)
gates.invalidates: the comparison BETWEEN arms, which is the entire experiment: alpha_a is a difference across BN and cannot survive the references moving 40x between them

gates.name: V4 ladders are readable
gates.prediction: quiet, monotone ladders and stable membership
gates.rule: across-repeat spread <= 2%, zero inversions beyond 2 sigma, every cell surviving >= 50% of bootstrap draws
gates.observed: spread BN=32:0.188%, BN=64:0.250%, BN=128:0.357%; 0 inversion(s); 0 unstable cell(s)
gates.invalidates: the fitted slopes, which are what alpha is: OLS gives the last tread the most leverage, and a cell whose membership flips between draws has a sigma conditioned on surviving

gates.name: V5 identifiability
gates.prediction: at least 3 BN values survive with an alpha
gates.rule: >= 3 distinct BN, and > 3 cells in total so the pooled fit keeps a degree of freedom
gates.invalidates: C1, C2, C3 and C4 alike: with two BN points and two unknowns the fit is exact, the residual is identically zero, and the model cannot be tested at all
lines: the primary BLOCK_M=128 carries 0 BN value(s). The parallel-branch tolerance is the predicted reason for a shortfall there and it is not a defect in the run: |B/C - 1| at 128 is predicted at 0.10 on the A100 against a tolerance of 0.15.

IT IS NO LONGER ONLY A PREDICTION. On 2026-09-10 the primary carried ZERO BN values on the H200: every BLOCK_M=128 cell at every BLOCK_N had its memory branch discarded, so this gate's shortfall clause is the arm's normal state and not its bad day. BLOCK_M=16 is swept because a fit over the two heights that survived cannot separate the activation column from the 1/BN column that beats it.

gates.name: C6 estimator sharpness
gates.prediction: alpha_a's interval is tighter than the two-point reading it replaces
gates.rule: bootstrap sd(alpha_a) <= 0.025, inside the 0.043 sd of the sharpest two-point slope this three-point fit replaces. That sd is the DECLARED prior over the pair's ds and is PINNED there, so a measured cross-arm floor does not lower this bar and does not make the two-point reading sharper than it was registered at. NOT half the band width either: the band is 0.28 wide and half of it would be a looser bar than the reading being replaced
gates.invalidates: C1 ALONE, which reads UNKNOWN: an estimator whose interval is wider than the hypothesis it tests has not tested it, and a PASS would be an artefact of the band's width. alpha_b, C3 and C5 do not pass through this spread and stay quotable
lines: 1000 draws, repeats resampled with replacement, whole chain re-decided per draw (reference, refusals, membership, alpha)
the bar is read from BM=64 of mixtral-8x7b-bf16-r1024-g1-n64-d66ad3.report.json vs mixtral-8x7b-bf16-r1024-g1-n256-16cc16.report.json

gates.name: C1 alpha_a
gates.observed: alpha_a = -0.8753 +/- 0.0619 -- UNKNOWN, not scored: C6 says the interval is too wide
lines: alpha_a band [0.10, 0.38], derived from the ONLY pair of committed arms that differ in BLOCK_SIZE_N and nothing else:
source: mixtral-8x7b-bf16-r1024-g1-n64-d66ad3.report.json vs mixtral-8x7b-bf16-r1024-g1-n256-16cc16.report.json

every +/- above is the DECLARED prior 0.0229, times sqrt(2) for the difference of two arms, divided by that pair's ds. It is PINNED to the declared number and deliberately NOT re-read from a measured floor: a pre-registration that moves when new information arrives is not one, so this band and the C6 bar built on it stay where they were registered even after part (a) publishes. What a measured floor moves is what the run can RESOLVE, which is the MDE and the cross-arm floor printed beside every interval below.

the band is 0.28 wide against input sds of 0.043-0.086, i.e. 3.2-6.5x the spread of the numbers that built it. A PASS inside it is weak evidence; a FAIL outside it is not. Narrowing it is what a three-point BN fit is for, which is this run.

A FAIL ABOVE the band with a clean residual would say both committed two-point slopes were biased low by the denominator the two-point form drops; a FAIL at or near zero says BN does not move alpha at all and there is no activation re-read to decompose. A PASS is weak: the two slopes above disagree by a factor of two and the band covers both, which is the width a three-point fit is here to narrow.

gates.prediction: alpha_b is the same at every BLOCK_M

lines: A FAIL above 1 is not a fitting artefact to be clipped: it says the per-M-tile cost divided by the weight bytes contains traffic the three terms do not name, which is C2's verdict arriving without a residual.

gates.name: C4 alpha_b against TEMPO
gates.rule: within 15% of the nearer TEMPO value
gates.observed: alpha_b = 0.9747 +/- 0.0037, nearest TEMPO value off by 205.6%
lines: THIS RUN IS PINNED AT GROUP_SIZE_M=16 and alpha_b is a property of that swizzle, not of the kernel. The study's earlier 0.307, and its '2-4% from TEMPO', are WITHDRAWN: that number was ALPHA_BY_BLOCK_M solved through (LIN), a unit artefact of reading a B/(A+B) fit as if it divided by weight bytes alone, not a measurement of alpha_b; through (EXA) the same G=1 ladders read alpha_b near 0.92, which is what 'consecutive M-tiles of one expert are scheduled far apart and the L2 keeps nothing' should look like. It was also pooled over GROUP_SIZE_M 1, 8, 16 and 64, which swing alpha by 0.39. So a FAIL at G=1 does NOT refute TEMPO, and a PASS at any G is the first number in this study that may be compared with TEMPO at all. Re-run at --group-m 16 to compare like with like.
